body.x: AIZEN Global (CEO Jung Seok Kang) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

AIZEN Global has contributed to global transition to low-carbon future and green financing through its CreditConnect, an AI Banking-as-a-Service platform. It predicts the residual value of previously non-measurable electric batteries and transparently measures associated financial risks to create new financial opportunities in the EV (Electric Vehicle) industry. The startup’s collaboration with banks from home and abroad to realize green financing demonstrates the reliability and sustainability of its financial services.

AIZEN Global decided to participate in this CES to share challenges and opportunities facing the U.S. on its transition to EV, and to identify potential partners who could create the global EV ecosystem.

CreditConnect that is to be introduced during the exhibition accurately and transparently predicts the residual value of batteries, which accounts for 40 – 50% of the cost in the BEV industry. Based on this capability, the offering provides key loan services ranging from BEV loan product design to portfolio management, battery risk management (i.e., SoH), and RV risk monitoring. The service provides a standardized risk management framework for BEV, and is expected to contribute to the global zero-emission policy and green financing in the future.

According to an AIZEN Global representative, “Despite the growing interest in green and sustainable finance, the banking industry are conservative toward BEV finance for a variety of reasons such as difficulty in measuring and predicting the residual value of BEV, lack of standardized product development and risk management policies for new EV finance, high initial costs and limited internal technology capabilities, and outdated legacy systems among others.”

They emphasized, “With our AI technology, we are able to address these issues by providing key loan services from loan product design to portfolio management, battery risk management, and risk monitoring.”

Since the first launch of CreditConnect BEV in South Korea in 2022, the startup has partnered with Korean battery platform businesses to develop an ML-based battery residual value prediction system using real-time battery data, providing the funds to purchase more than 150 electric buses. Currently, AIZEN Global is conducting projects to supply 50,000 electric bicycles to Indonesia by 2023 with overseas e-mobility and battery exchange platform companies, expanding its services beyond the domestic market to global ones. As part of this effort, AIZEN Global revealed its plan to launch the CreditConnect EV USA service, targeting buses and last mile mobility operators.

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
